assumptions: 'Unless otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control signal' cannot be seen by the camera and is excluded from the check.
'shall stop' is interpreted as continuously stopped with speed <=0.05 for at least 1000 ms, as no duration is stated.
'at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line' is interpreted as inside stop_zone, the last 10 metres before the stop line.
Inbound approach direction is interpreted as to_right per the stop_line definition (y<0.6 to y>0.6, +y = to_right).
Anchor center is used because boxes are vehicles viewed from above where centre is metric position and bottom_center is downstream AABB edge, not wheels.
Vehicles that never cross the stop line pass vacuously; only vehicles that cross are required to have stopped before.
No maximum time limit is imposed between the stop and the crossing.
raw_output.normalized_explanation: Every vehicle that crosses the stop line inbound must first come to a complete stop inside the approach waiting zone.

provenance.quote: at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line

provenance.reason: The statute requires a stop but states no minimum duration; 1000 ms is assumed as the minimum continuously-stopped interval observable as a stop.

provenance.quote: at a clearly marked stop line

provenance.reason: The statute only says 'approaching'; inbound approach (y<0.6 to y>0.6, +y) is defined as to_right for this line, so to_right is assumed to enforce approach direction.
Boxes are vehicles viewed from above where centre is metric position while bottom_center is downstream AABB edge, not wheels, so centre is the point the zone and line were drawn for.
The statute states no maximum time between the stop and the crossing, so no time limit is imposed.

text: Unless otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control signal, the driver of a vehicle approaching a stop sign at an intersection shall stop at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line.
